info.bio:
John Mellencamp, también conocido como John Cougar o John Cougar Mellencamp, (nacido el 7 Octubre de 1951) es un autor e interprete de Rock Americano. Empezó llamándose John Cougar, nombre que cambió posteriormente a Cougar Mellencamp para acabar definitivamente con sólo Mellencamp.

John Mellencamp comenzó su carrera a finales de los 70 (de 1976 es su primer disco, que resultó un fracaso comercial); su popularidad se fue acrecentando aprovechando el tirón de la música de Bruce Springsteen

scenes.desc: La emancipación definitiva de la mujer en el rock (Terry Garthwaite, Joan Armatrading, Nanci Griffith y, sobre todo, Rickie Lee Jones, protegida de Tom Waits); la escuela tejana de cantautores herederos de Townes Van Zandt (Guy Clark, Butch Hancock, Joe Ely, Terry Allen, Rodney Crowell, T-Bone Burnett); el populismo melancólico de la posguerra de Vietnam (Warren Zevon, Rick Danko, Steve Forbert, John Hiatt, John Mellencamp, Don Henley, Donald Fagen, Robbie Robertson); y el puente de 1977 hacia la new wave: Peter Gabriel, poeta atormentado de las neurosis postindustriales, Marianne Faithfull y Kate Bush.

podcast.title: Criticism of The Babys (1980)
podcast.body: In December 1980, Mellencamp, then known as John Cougar Mellencamp (after going by Johnny Cougar), told a reporter for the San Francisco Examiner that The Babys were "a bullshit band," specifically targeting their song "Every Time I Think of You." "John Melanchamp, then known as John Cougar Melanchamp, after going by Johnny Cougar, told a reporter for the San Francisco Examiner that the babies were quote, a bullshit band."

podcast.title: Self-Assessment of Own Hits (1980)
podcast.body: Mellencamp considered his own 1980 hits, "This Time" and "Ain't Even Done With The Night," to be "stupid little pop records." He desired to make rock music for a specific group, feeling he and The Babys were falling short. "Melanchamp, who by the way, thought that his own hits from 1980 this time and even Della Muthanite were what he called stupid little pop records."

podcast.title: "Heartland Rock" Label Dislike
podcast.body: Mellencamp, an Indiana native from Seymour, has consistently expressed his dislike for the "Heartland Rock" label, partly due to its political connotations. He identifies as liberal, contrasting with Indiana's conservative "red state" status, and believes his songs would be vastly different if he truly were "the voice of the heartland." "They didn't hang it on Bob Seger at least not that I know of and he writes about the same shit as me it was never true first of all the heartland is very conservative in the United States Indiana is a red state. And you're looking at the most liberal motherfucker you know if I was the voice of the heartland my songs would have been vastly different."

podcast.title: Concert Ticket Sales Comparison
podcast.body: The Tragically Hip's Canadian tour for *Fully Completely* achieved such popularity that in some cities, tickets sold out faster than those for John Mellencamp, indicating The Hip's significant draw at the time. "The supporting Canadian tour sold out in minutes and in some cities the hip sold out faster than Rod Stewart and John Mellon Camp."

podcast.title: Farm Aid Association
podcast.body: Mellencamp forever cemented his image as a "heartland rocker" who spoke for the "downtrodden common man" through his strong association with Farm Aid. This organization, which he co-founded, came into existence two months after Live Aid and continues its work today. "He forever cemented that interpretation of his music with his association with far made which came into existence two months after live aid and unlike live aid it still exists today."

podcast.title: Imperial Capital for Rootsy Rock
podcast.body: Known in the 80s as John Cougar Mellencamp, he leveraged his imperial peak after the success of "Scarecrow" (1985) to release "The Lonesome Jubilee" (1987), an album infused with folk and country instruments. This allowed him to score a top 10 pop hit ("Paper in Fire") with a "rootsy folk rock" sound that was otherwise incongruous with the prevailing chart trends. "John Melanchamp had imperial capital and he spent it to get rootsy folk rock on the radio."

podcast.title: Interracial Couple Revisited in Video
podcast.body: After his record company overruled the original concept of "Jack & Diane" being about an interracial couple in 1982, Mellencamp revisited this topic in the music video for his 1987 song "Cherry Bomb." "he would revisit that topic again in the cherry bomb video in 1987 if you have not seen it or haven't seen it for a while head on over to YouTube and as melanchamp says check it out."

podcast.title: Name Changes and Image
podcast.body: In 1982, Mellencamp was known as John Cougar because his manager believed "Mellencamp" didn't sound like a rock star's name. Although he was sometimes called "Johnny Cougar," he stated that nobody ever called him Johnny in real life, indicating that "Johnny" was part of an imposed image rather than a genuine identity. "In that 1982 top 10 list I just read melanchamp was still going by john cougar because his manager didn't think melanchamp sounded like a rock stars name he had those two songs hurt so good and jack and Diane he was actually johnny cougar although he said nobody ever called him johnny in his life it was all this image that they were trying to."

"With Dan's help Malcolm has had gigs producing an engineering for Iggy Pop and Patty Smith and Bob Dylan and Blue Road View and Midnight Oil and junk house and John Mellon Camp in many many more."

xref.title: Sales Success of Fully Completely Canadian Tour
xref.body: The Canadian tour in support of *Fully Completely* achieved remarkable success, with tickets selling out within minutes in numerous cities. The demand was so high that in some locations, The Tragically Hip's tickets sold out faster than those for established artists like Rod Stewart and John Mellencamp. "The supporting Canadian tour sold out in minutes and in some cities the hip sold out faster than Rod Stewart and John Mellon Camp."
